decision: Includes inside remote content: a `file:` include resolves against the containing URL and is fetched; nested http(s) includes are allowed; a URL cycle exits 4; everything reached this way is read-only
options: (A) resolve file: against the URL, allow nested remote includes
(B) allow https includes, refuse file: inside remote content
(C) no includes in remote content at all
reason: Keeps the step-1 meaning of a relative include for remote files; a shared file cannot sensibly point at a path on each user's disk

decision: A reference in remote content that resolves outside http(s) is refused (exit 4); a scheme-relative `file://host/x` resolves to http(s)://host/x by standard URL rules
reason: It gives nothing a remote file could not name directly (post-merge review R-c)

decision: Settle the remaining out-of-contract points itself and offer them for one round of confirmation, rather than asking about each one
options: bundle the agent choices into one confirmation
reason: Most of what remains is outside the contract

decision: Fetch every remote include fresh on every load with no cache between runs; each URL is fetched at most once per load
reason: Files are already read fresh on every run; a cache could show stale shared values

decision: Fetch timeout of 10 seconds, as one total deadline across the whole fetch
options: environment variable to set the timeout
reason: Keeps a dead server from hanging every command; a configurable timeout would be a configuration surface nobody asked for

decision: The 10 s deadline also bounds DNS lookup (run in a daemon thread), every connect attempt, the TLS handshake and every read
options: fix only the connect timeout reported by the reviewer
reason: WP01 review reproduced a 20-second fetch; a full fix makes the 'never more than 10 s' claim hold without exceptions

decision: Redirects are followed only to http/https targets; any other scheme is a failed fetch
reason: Stops redirects from reaching file:// URLs and reading local files (challenge A-2)

decision: Check the redirect scheme in http_error_30x rather than redirect_request
reason: urllib rejects file: targets before redirect_request with an HTTPError that reads like a status failure, and it would even follow ftp:

decision: Verify TLS certificates, send no credentials or cookies; the body must be strict UTF-8 with no newline translation
reason: Refusing an unverified or undecodable response cannot corrupt anything (TROUPE-002)

decision: The YAML-or-text decision for a URL uses the URL path only (query and fragment ignored), with the same case-sensitive .yml/.yaml test
A failed fetch exits 4 and names the URL plus the location holding the include (the local file, or the remote URL for a nested include)
reason: Aligned with contracts/cli.md after post-merge finding D-3

decision: Use only the standard library's urllib.request for fetching
reason: Covers redirects, TLS verification and timeouts with no new dependency

decision: Honour proxies from the environment, as urllib does by default
Ignore any charset in Content-Type; keep a leading BOM in the text, as for local files; any 2xx is success and a 204 yields an empty string; keep urllib's cap on the number of redirects
reason: S-2 says the body must be UTF-8

decision: $ref mapping form accepts remote includes with overrides; a $ref value is always an include, and !literal on it exits 4
reason: New keys under a remote include become local overrides, which needs the mapping form; a non-include $ref was already refused in step 5

decision: Read-only scope: changing a remote value, replacing a remote include, --in-include into remote content, appending to a remote list or adding a key in a remote list item, and --expand-alias in remote content all exit 3, quoting the outermost local include string
reason: These are every write that would otherwise land in remote content; only a line in a local file can be changed

decision: Enforce read-only with one guard (placement.remote_refusal) at two checkpoints (after walk, before alias routing; and on the planned files), plus an assertion in write_files
options: a check in every placement branch
reason: With about eight branches one could be missed; checkpoint 2 looks at what would actually be written

decision: New keys under a remote include become local overrides, using the step-5 scalar-to-mapping conversion; the step-6 alias refusal still applies
reason: Contract plus step-5 conversion and step-6 ruling C6

decision: Remote changes on the server are recorded at the next reconcile as file-lineage events; watch does not poll URLs and reconciles only when local files or the schema file change
options: (A) record like a hand edit at the next reconcile
(B) watch also polls URLs on a slower interval
(C) keep remote leaves out of history
reason: Keeps history complete, adds no polling, and reuses the existing reconcile rule

decision: While the configuration cannot load, watch keeps retrying on every tick, re-fetching a failing remote include each time
options: back off to at most every 10 s (proposed in discovery run)
keep step-3 retry on every tick
reason: Existing step-3 behaviour (analysis finding I1)

decision: show --sources attributes remote scalars to the resolved URL

Schema lookup walks properties, additionalProperties (when it is an object) and items only; $ref, combinators, patternProperties and prefixItems are not followed; for aliased strings the anchored node's path decides
reason: The contract names exactly these keywords; following more would guess at the meaning of combinators

decision: Each schema step carries its container kind (mapping or list)
reason: A segment like "0" could be either

decision: Schema is read fresh each load and must be strict UTF-8 JSON (NaN/Infinity refused), valid 2020-12, $schema naming 2020-12 if present, and every $ref/$dynamicRef must be a local fragment; format is not asserted; the resolved configuration is what gets validated
reason: Matches 'the loaded configuration must validate'; 2020-12 treats format as an annotation; not fetching references keeps loading offline-safe

decision: The first reported violation is ordered by smallest JSON path (key name, numeric indexes), then shortest path, then validator name
reason: Deterministic; the spec does not fix an order (post-merge finding D-1 corrected the research wording)

decision: Add jsonschema (Draft202012Validator, empty Registry, no format checker) as a runtime dependency
reason: A subtly wrong hand-written validator would accept or refuse configurations against the contract; fastjsonschema's 2020-12 support is incomplete; owner said take the safest assumption

decision: Set no-build-package for rpds-py so uv never builds it from source
reason: A source build would run arbitrary build code (challenge A-5)

decision: Skip the multi-agent challenge squad and do a single-reviewer challenge pass
reason: The only security-relevant dependency decision was directed by the owner and is covered by supply-chain mitigations

decision: A set whose result fails validation exits 3 naming PATH and the schema file
reason: Contract; refusing before writing cannot corrupt anything

decision: Validate in a separate configuration.load_configuration entry point, not inside loader.load
reason: A set needs a different exit code (3) for the same violation

decision: Reuse fetched remote content across all reloads within one command
reason: The command's own reloads cannot fail on a remote change mid-command

decision: !literal allowed on scalars of any style (value is the text as a string); on mapping/list exits 4; other tags exit 4; get/show print without tag; anchors allowed on literals; !literal on a mapping key exits 4
reason: Only scalars are strings; reads print values, not file syntax; keys are never includes (analysis U1)

decision: Record the !literal tag span in the composer and move the scalar start past the tag
options: strip tag text out in the writers
reason: Otherwise span knowledge would spread across about eight writers and a rewrite would delete the tag

decision: Every include-looking string in a set VALUE, including nested ones, is written as !literal, judged at its own path; an existing tag is kept when the new value is a string; text-include content is never tagged
reason: A nested string would otherwise become an unwanted include; keeping a tag keeps the user's intent and changes the fewest bytes

decision: Use LiteralStr/IncludeStr str-subclass markers to carry literal/include intent to renderers
options: pass a per-path predicate down every renderer
reason: A str subclass travels unchanged through renderers; the alternative changes about 15 signatures

decision: --include only on set (exit 2 elsewhere); no effect on values that are not include-looking; exit 3 if the new include cannot be read or fetched, or if PATH is format: uri; removes an existing !literal tag
reason: Mirrors --in-include/--expand-alias; writing an unloadable include would break the configuration (analysis U2)

decision: Change step-1 behaviour so set b file:p.md writes !literal, and update the two existing tests to pass --include
reason: The contract requires it

decision: Introduce Location = Path | Url and retype SourceFile.path while keeping the field name
reason: mypy flags every disk-only use; a rename would touch about 10 modules for no gain

decision: Centralise the include rule in a new includes.py module
reason: TROUPE-007; apply.py and value tagging also need it

decision: Alias copies via --expand-alias keep the !literal tag
reason: Otherwise a copy of a literal would become a remote include

decision: Tags other than !literal keep the step-6 error message
reason: So existing tests don't change

decision: No-op check: an include node matches only an IncludeStr; a literal ScalarNode matches only a non-IncludeStr string
reason: Otherwise repeating an existing include string inside a collection would wrongly be a no-op

decision: Test remote content against a local threaded HTTP server with a request log; test TLS with an openssl self-signed certificate, skipped with a reason if openssl is missing
reason: TROUPE-005 and offline tests (C-006)

decision: Initially set no size limit on fetched bodies
reason: The spec doesn't ask for one; don't invent one

decision: Limit each fetched body to 1 MiB, checked against Content-Length and again while reading
reason: Configurations are small; an unbounded body could exhaust memory; refusing cannot lose data

decision: Refuse https to http redirects at every hop; still follow http to https and same-scheme redirects
reason: Following a downgrade would silently drop the encryption the owner asked for

decision: No warning for http:// includes
reason: The contract makes http:// a normal include; a warning would add stderr noise with no contract basis

decision: WP05 fix: anchor identity goes back to the written path while schema lookups stay at the merge mount point, reaching the merge source through MergeKeyMapping.written
reason: A loader change had let a set silently change an unrelated value through a shared YAML anchor; the path lookup goes through a merge view that hides <<

decision: WP08 fix: run the read-only check before edit rendering
reason: Read-only refusals could come with the wrong error message

decision: Resume stopped implementer agents from their saved transcripts rather than restarting them
reason: Uncommitted work was intact in the worktrees

decision: Resolve the planning-file conflict during workspace creation using the planning branch's version
reason: Only the planning file conflicted

decision: Finish WP06/WP07 itself and run the full suites as detached processes logging to files
reason: Sessions kept ending before long jobs could finish

decision: Leave the parent issue 1j5 open rather than force-closing it
reason: The tracker won't close a parent while its children are open

decision: Run acceptance with --mission and --lenient after fast-forwarding the feature branch to main, without creating a docs/ directory
reason: Followed what the previous mission did in the same situation

decision: Leave the mission coordination branch in place
reason: Its worktree is still checked out, and earlier missions left theirs

decision: Commit the plan-document amendments and the status bookkeeping as two separate commits
reason: Precedent from commit 297995b
